structure.title: IV.A-B Effectiveness of Defection Messaging; Aggregate Effects

observations.statement: The identification strategy is stated as resting on three sources of plausibly exogenous variation: topography-driven variation in radio signal reception, cell-level panel fixed effects, and the random overlap of multiple radio signals used to build a message-intensity measure.
observations.quote: we rely on three sources of plausibly exogenous variation

observations.statement: Because individual reception of radio messages cannot be observed, the authors state that their coefficient should be interpreted as an intention-to-treat effect of defection messaging rather than a per-recipient effect.
observations.quote: we can interpret estimates as an intention-to-treat effect of defection messaging

observations.statement: The paper argues against endogenous antenna placement as a threat to identification by controlling for distance from active antennas (and its square), the median distance from all active antennas, and interactions of distance with terrain ruggedness, labeled collectively as propagation controls.
observations.quote: we rule out the possibility of endogenous location of antennas by controlling for distance from active antennas

observations.statement: Exogeneity of the messaging-intensity measure is checked directly using household survey data, testing whether pre-existing village characteristics predict the future intensity of messaging; this check is reported only in a footnote rather than the main text body.

The authors explicitly address a reverse-causality concern, that radio operators might have expanded messaging in anticipation of a future reduction in violence, and state that they do not find evidence supporting this alternative channel.

The unit of observation is a fixed grid of equally sized cells overlaid on the conflict-affected territory rather than administrative units, chosen to avoid the endogeneity of political boundaries to violence and to permit cell-specific fixed effects.

The analysis period is restricted to the years following the described military dispersal of the insurgent group, justified by the concurrent start of a detailed event-tracking database and by the concentration of the messaging campaign's expansion in that later window.

The radio-station survey covers the full set of stations broadcasting defection content during the study window; a footnote notes that data on stations active before that window were also collected but excluded from the analysis because the earlier information was judged unreliable.

Events are aggregated to the cell-year level rather than analyzed at their exact reported location and date, a choice explicitly justified as reducing measurement error arising from imprecise event geocoding and timing.

Every main results table reports the number of observations and the number of cells beneath the coefficient block for each specification, but none of the main tables report R-squared or the dependent-variable mean.

The treatment variable, intensity of messaging, is defined by an explicit equation as the coverage-weighted sum of daily broadcast minutes across all radios reaching a cell, and is standardized in every specification to ease interpretation of the coefficient.

Radio signal coverage is corrected for topography using an established terrain-propagation model applied to each station's technical parameters, following the same modeling approach used by prior media-and-violence studies, at a stated fine spatial resolution.

The main conflict-count outcomes are log-transformed after adding a small constant to accommodate zero-valued cells, with an alternative additive constant, a square-root transform, levels, and a binary extensive-margin indicator all reported as alternative functional forms of the same outcome.

Commodity price-shock variables combine each cell's historical share of land farmed with a given crop and the year-over-year change in that commodity's international price, following an established construction from the economic-shocks-and-conflict literature.

The set of time-varying controls entering the benchmark specification, and the two commodities used for the heterogeneity analysis, are chosen via Lasso regression over a longer candidate list rather than selected ex ante by the authors.

The benchmark specification is explicitly defined in the table notes as cell and year fixed effects, propagation controls, commodity-price and weather-shock controls, and macro-region-by-year fixed effects.

Within a single table, numbered rows progress from a minimal fixed-effects-only model to the benchmark and then to variants adding cell-specific trends or a circular-coverage control, rather than presenting each variant as a separate table or column.

The type of standard error used (a correction allowing correlation over time and space) is stated once in the table notes rather than being discussed inline alongside individual coefficients in the text.

Standard errors are computed using a spatial-HAC correction attributed to Conley and Hsiang, explicitly justified by concern for both serial correlation within a cell over time and spatial correlation across nearby cells.

The text states that results are robust to alternative spatial cutoffs for the HAC correction and to conventional clustering at the cell or district level, but these alternative inference approaches are shown only in the online appendix.
The spatial-HAC correction is implemented using code adapted from a named prior study, credited explicitly in a footnote rather than described from first principles in the main text.

A placebo diagnostic randomly reassigns antenna locations across many simulated draws and re-estimates the benchmark model; the main text summarizes an average null finding across the simulations while the full simulation results are reported only in an online appendix table.

An indirect exogeneity check tests whether pre-existing household characteristics from a household survey predict the future intensity of messaging in a village, functioning as a balance-style diagnostic but described only in a footnote.

A circular-coverage falsification control (predicted signal reach absent topographic obstruction) is added to the benchmark specification and shown to have no independent effect and only a low correlation with the topography-based treatment, offered as evidence that topographic variation rather than simple distance drives identification.

Spillover diagnostics using two additional conflict datasets test whether messaging affects violence unrelated to the targeted armed group; detailed tables supporting this null-spillover claim are placed only in the online appendix.

A diagnostic check rules out a contemporaneous increase in military activity as an alternative explanation for reduced violence, using the same alternative conflict datasets, with detail placed in the online appendix.

A set of alternative control-set specifications, ranging from a minimal fixed-effects model through the benchmark to variants adding cell-specific trends or circular coverage, is stacked as rows within the main results table rather than presented in a separate robustness table.

Alternative definitions of the treatment variable, an average-intensity-per-station measure and a simple percent-coverage measure that ignores message frequency, are substituted into the benchmark specification within the same main table.

The benchmark specification is re-estimated under several alternative functional forms of the dependent variable within the same table, to show that results are not an artifact of the chosen log transformation.

Nonlinear count-data estimators are mentioned in the main text as an additional robustness check on functional form but the corresponding estimates are reported only in an online appendix table, not reproduced in the main text.

Two robustness panels in a dedicated table separately add controls for an alternative mobile-communication technology and for general, non-defection FM radio coverage, to rule out confounding by other media technologies.

The paper states that replacing grid cells with administrative district boundaries as the unit of analysis leaves the paper's conclusions unaffected, with the underlying comparison shown only in the online appendix.

Robustness is also assessed across a range of area fixed-effects structures, from no area fixed effects up to the full cell fixed-effects specification, summarized narratively as confirming that both temporal and topographic variation contribute to the estimated effect, with full results in the online appendix.

Heterogeneity by economic shocks is estimated through interaction terms added directly to the benchmark specification (shock variables interacted with the treatment), rather than by splitting the sample into subgroups.

The continuous treatment variable is discretized into several intensity-interval dummy variables to visualize a nonlinear dose-response pattern in a coefficient plot, with the zero-messaging interval serving as the excluded reference category.

The two commodities used for the heterogeneity interaction analysis are selected through the same Lasso procedure used for the control set, rather than chosen a priori by the authors, and this selection is described as following an objective criterion.

A battery of cross-sectional heterogeneity splits, by country, distance to border, terrain ruggedness, climate variables, and economic-prosperity proxies, is summarized narratively in the main text while the full set of underlying estimates is relegated to the online appendix.

Heterogeneity by messaging content type and by broadcast language is explored specifically to distinguish between the two persuasion channels, belief-based and preference-based, laid out in the introduction's conceptual framework.

A reduction in events characterized as violence against civilians and clashes, alongside the reduction in fatalities, is interpreted as suggestive evidence that fewer attacks rather than less lethal attacks drive the fatality reduction, explicitly framed as one possible channel rather than a directly tested mechanism.

An increase in looting under more intense messaging is interpreted as a survival-oriented response by remaining members, supported by a disaggregation of looted-goods categories placed in the online appendix, with the authors describing the pattern as suggestive rather than as a definitive test of the channel.

The authors explicitly label their opportunity-cost/rapacity interpretation of the commodity-shock heterogeneity results as an ex post rationalization, stating plainly that the available data do not allow them to directly test the specific channel.
observations.quote: the discussion above is an ex post rationalization

observations.statement: Aggregate impact is interpreted through counterfactual predicted outcomes constructed from a more flexible functional-form model described in the online appendix, rather than by simple linear extrapolation of the benchmark coefficient.

Effect sizes are consistently interpreted in terms of a one-standard-deviation change in the standardized treatment variable at full cell coverage, and are also re-expressed in terms of daily messaging minutes so the standardized coefficient has a directly interpretable policy meaning.

The authors acknowledge that conflict-event reporting may correlate with local media coverage, but argue that this measurement error should bias estimates toward understating rather than overstating the messaging effect.

Because individual reception of messages cannot be observed, the authors explicitly limit their causal claim to an intention-to-treat interpretation rather than asserting a per-recipient treatment effect.
The authors state directly that their economic-channel narrative for the commodity-shock heterogeneity results is an ex post rationalization that the available data do not permit testing directly.
observations.quote: available data do not allow testing of specific channels in the LRA setting

observations.statement: The conclusion frames the intervention as a generalizable low-cost counterinsurgency tool for remote, low-state-capacity conflicts, pointing to an online appendix section cataloguing other conflicts where similar radio messaging has been used, rather than presenting cross-context estimates in the main text.

The empirical presentation opens with a descriptive-statistics table reporting the mean, standard deviation, minimum, maximum and observation count for each variable, split into an antenna-level panel and a cell-level panel, before any regression table appears.
Coefficient estimates throughout the main tables are reported without significance stars; precision is conveyed only through parenthetical standard errors placed directly beneath each coefficient.
Nonlinear treatment-response and interaction effects are presented as coefficient plots with stated confidence intervals rather than as additional columns in a regression table.

Spatial patterns in conflict incidence, radio coverage, and messaging intensity are visualized as choropleth maps drawn on a common basemap across several figures spread through the data and results sections.
The reference list cites a replication data package deposited with a data archive under its own DOI, but the main text itself contains no separate data-and-code-availability statement or section.

The analysis panel combines an original primary survey of radio-station characteristics and messaging content with several secondary public-use event and geographic databases assembled by NGOs and other outside sources, merged at the cell-year level.

The acknowledgments state that ethics approval for the study, including the ex-combatant survey component, was obtained from a named university ethics board under a specific application reference, but no pre-analysis plan or preregistration is mentioned anywhere in the text.
The introduction previews the paper's main pattern of quantitative findings, across fatalities, returnees and other conflict outcomes, before the data or empirical-strategy sections are presented.
The data section is placed before the empirical-strategy section, so that all data sources are described before the estimating equation is formally introduced.

The introduction closes with an explicit contribution structure, separately positioning the paper against three distinct literatures (media and violence, counterinsurgency, and DDR/amnesty policy) in turn before the paper moves to background.
Robustness checks are placed as the final lettered subsection within the single numbered Results section rather than being given a standalone top-level section of their own.

The paper is heavily appendix-reliant: nearly every robustness check, heterogeneity split, and diagnostic mentioned in the main text points to a specific online appendix section or table rather than reproducing the full results in the printed paper.

concordance.paper_says: The benchmark model is described as a fixed-effects panel regression with cell and year fixed effects (equation 2), consistent with a linear fixed-effects panel estimator.
concordance.card_shows: Both extracted specifications record estimator=hdfe_ols: s1 via Stata command xtreg (fe robust) and s2 via reg2hdfespatial (spatial HAC).

concordance.paper_says: The paper explicitly states cell and year fixed effects plus macro-region-by-year fixed effects for the benchmark specification.
concordance.card_shows: The fixed_effects field is null for both s1 and s2; the code-engineer did not extract the FE structure from the do-file macros.

concordance.paper_says: Main-table standard errors are described as allowing for correlation over time and space, following a named spatial-HAC correction (Conley, Hsiang).
concordance.card_shows: se.type=conley_spatial is recorded for s2 (CONLEY.do), matching the main tables' description; a separate s1 (ROBUST.do) records se.type=robust.

concordance.paper_says: No discrete cluster level is reported; inference relies on a continuous spatial-temporal HAC correction rather than clustering on a grouping variable.
concordance.card_shows: se.cluster_level is null for both s1 and s2.

concordance.paper_says: The estimation sample is described as a cell-year panel covering the full study area over the stated sample period, with observation and cell counts reported per table.
concordance.card_shows: The sample field is null for both s1 and s2.

concordance.paper_says: The control set is described as Lasso-selected commodity-price and weather shocks plus a defined set of propagation controls for antenna distance and terrain ruggedness.
concordance.card_shows: controls_summary is null for both s1 and s2; only the unresolved $trends and $dist macros are flagged.

concordance.paper_says: No observation-weighting scheme for the panel regressions is mentioned anywhere in the main text.
concordance.card_shows: The weights field is also null for both specifications.
concordance.note: Both paper and code are silent, so absence of weighting cannot be distinguished from unstated equal weighting.

concordance.paper_says: The paper's design diagnostics are a randomized antenna-placement placebo test and a household-survey-based exogeneity check, not a classic temporal pre-trends plot (the design is cross-sectional/topographic, not an event study).
concordance.card_shows: The card's only diagnostic record (x1) reports a pre-trends plot as not_found_in_scope, with a note that the spatial design relies on topography rather than temporal pre-trends.
concordance.note: The card correctly anticipates the absence of a pre-trends plot but does not capture the placebo-antenna or survey-based diagnostics the paper actually reports.

concordance.paper_says: Table 2 panel B reports the benchmark specification under alternative functional forms of the dependent variable (an alternative log constant, square root, levels, and an extensive-margin indicator).
concordance.card_shows: The robustness array records an alt_functional_form check (log(y+0.5), square root, levels) with baseline spec s2, extracted from CONLEY.do.

concordance.paper_says: Table 2, titled "Effect of Defection Messaging on Fatalities," is the paper's main results table for the fatalities outcome.
concordance.card_shows: outputs.tables record t1 is labeled "Table 2 (main)" with matching evidence from the CONLEY.do table header.

concordance.paper_says: The core conflict data are described as coming from an NGO-run event-tracking project (the LRA Crisis Tracker), supplemented by an original station survey and by other public NGO/administrative geographic databases, not primarily by government administrative records.
concordance.card_shows: The merged dataset file (Radio_LRA_DB125.dta) is labeled with type=admin.
concordance.note: The paper characterizes the LRACT source as an NGO-curated crisis-tracking database rather than administrative data; the card's admin label may reflect a coarse code-engineer classification convention rather than the paper's own description of the source.

gaps: Main results tables report observation and cell counts for every specification but do not report R-squared or the dependent-variable mean, despite otherwise detailed table notes.
No pre-analysis plan or preregistration is mentioned; only IRB/ethics approval for the survey component is stated (preregistration_or_ethics is otherwise unobserved).
No explicit statement of estimation software appears in the main text; software use is only inferable from the replication-package citation in the references, not from the text itself.
No discussion of observation weighting for the panel regressions appears in either the main text or the table notes.
No explicit description of a discrete comparison group is given, consistent with the continuous-treatment design; the paper does not use control-group or comparison-group language.

reading.note: Read the entire extracted text end to end: title/abstract, introduction, background, data (subsections A-D), empirical strategy, all results subsections (IV.A effectiveness, IV.B aggregate effects, IV.C heterogeneity, IV.D robustness), conclusion, and the reference list. This file contains only the published 35-page main text; the paper's extensive online appendix, referenced repeatedly throughout for additional figures, tables and robustness detail, is a separate document not included in this extraction and was not read. Observations describing appendix content rely on the main text's own description of what the appendix contains.
